parts.text:
You read part of an interview. An analyst asked one future user of a software service a series of questions. You decide, for each question, whether it follows up the answer given just before it.

A question follows up the previous answer when it asks about something that answer said: it asks the speaker to explain, give an example of, say more about, or say why of something the answer mentioned, or it picks up a particular thing the answer named. Wording does not matter; a question can follow up an answer without repeating any of its words.

A question does not follow up the previous answer when it turns to something that answer did not mention, even if the speaker said it in an earlier answer, even if it stays with the same broad subject, and even if it is a good question. A general question that could follow any answer, such as whether there is anything else, does not follow up either.

You receive the pairs of the interview after its first question: for each later question, the answer given just before it, and the question.

Reply with JSON only: an object with one key, "questions", a list with exactly one entry for every pair, in the same order. Each entry has "id", the question's id, and "follow_up", true or false.

Q2
The answer just before it: I keep the drones and charging equipment in working order, which involves adding new drones to the fleet, retiring old ones, setting up charging pads at our sites, taking drones out of service for repairs and putting them back, and sending drones to charge. Regulators can ask us to show how our drones have been looked after, and our repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians. I do not know anything about software or what is needed from the new service.
The question: When you take a drone out of service for repair, what should happen to flights already planned for that drone, and to a flight it is flying right now? And who is allowed to put it back into service, under what conditions?

Q3
The answer just before it: I do not know how flights already planned or currently in flight are handled when I take a drone out of service. My notes state that I take drones out of service for repairs and put them back, and that repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians. However, my notes do not state any specific conditions for putting a drone back into service.
The question: Tell me about charging: how do you send a drone to charge, what are the limits of charging pads (how many drones at once, which connectors, which sites), and what goes wrong with charging today?

Q4
The answer just before it: I send drones to charge, and we have a few dozen charging pads at our own sites. Several connector types are in use, and they are not interchangeable, while our pads are never lent to another company. What goes wrong today is that the links used to give instructions to the charging equipment are unreliable, meaning an instruction may get through twice and the sender often cannot tell whether the first attempt arrived.
The question: When an instruction to the charging equipment gets through twice, or you cannot tell if it arrived, what harm does it cause, and how do you find out what the pad is really doing?

Q5
The answer just before it: I do not know what harm a duplicated or unconfirmed instruction causes. My notes do not say how I find out what the charging pad is really doing.
The question: What records must you be able to show regulators about how drones have been looked after, how far back, and are there rules about changing or deleting those records?

Q6
The answer just before it: Regulators can ask us to show how our drones have been looked after, and our repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians. My notes do not state how far back these records must go. My notes also state that none of the companies is seeking certification from the platform, and that there are no data-retention or deletion features.
The question: Are the technicians who repair and service your drones all your own company's staff, or do some outside or contract technicians (perhaps working for several companies) do this work? What may each see and do?

Q7
The answer just before it: I do not know whether the technicians who repair and service our drones are our own staff or outside contractors. My notes state that repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians, and that each company's fleet, jobs, sites, and problems are its own business.
The question: When you add a new drone to the fleet or retire one, what details do you record about it, and what should happen to a retired drone's history and to anything still planned for it?

Q8
The answer just before it: I add new drones to the fleet and retire old ones, but my notes do not state what details I record about them. My notes also do not say what should happen to a retired drone's history or to anything still planned for it.
The question: Besides repairs, what else do you know about drones that dispatchers need to know before using one (battery level, faults, servicing due, where it is)? And what problems do you have today working with dispatchers?

Q9
The answer just before it: I do not know what else dispatchers need to know before using a drone, or what problems I have working with them. My notes state that I keep drones and charging equipment in working order, add new drones to the fleet, retire old ones, set up charging pads at our sites, take drones out of service for repairs and put them back, and send drones to charge.
The question: Is there anything else you know about your work, the drones, sites, charging pads, batteries, or what the service must or must not do, that you have not yet told me? Please tell me everything.

Q10
The answer just before it: I keep our drones and charging equipment in working order, and our repairs and servicing are carried out by technicians. Regulators can ask our company to show how its drones have been looked after. I do not know anything about software or what the new service must or must not do.
The question: How does a drone's battery level, location and condition become known to you: does the drone or pad report it, do you enter it by hand, and can those reports be late, repeated or wrong like other reports?

Q11
The answer just before it: I do not know how a drone's battery level, location, and condition become known to me, or whether those reports can be late, repeated, or wrong. My notes state that reports from drones come through relay stations and can arrive late, out of order, more than once, or not at all, but they do not state whether this applies to battery level, location, or condition reports.
The question: May a dispatcher plan or sign off a flight for a drone that you have taken out of service or that is charging? And may you take a drone out of service or send it to charge without asking the dispatcher who has planned it?

Q12
The answer just before it: I do not know whether a dispatcher may plan or sign off a flight for a drone that I have taken out of service or that is charging. My notes do not state whether I may take a drone out of service or send it to charge without asking a dispatcher.
The question: When you set up a charging pad at a site, what do you record about it (site, connector type, how many drones it charges at once), and what should happen if you send a drone to a pad with the wrong connector, a busy pad, or a pad at another site?

Q13
The answer just before it: I set up charging pads at our company's sites, and we have a few dozen of them. Several connector types are in use, and they are not interchangeable. My notes do not state what I record when setting up a pad, or what should happen if I send a drone to a pad with the wrong connector, a busy pad, or a pad at another site.
The question: What does a drone's home site mean in practice: must it return there after flights, may it charge at any of your company's sites with a matching pad, and can its home site change?
